=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1350-1361 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In the `_gh_read_run` reason=error branch, when the PAT fallback also fails, line 1359 `rm -f "${out_file}" "${err_file}"` discards the PAT's stderr and lines 1360-1361 replay the job token's `err_text` and `${rc}`, so `gh_retry` only ever sees the job token's transient 5xx/network error.
  WHY: Permanent PAT failures (HTTP 404/400/401/422, "Bad credentials") never match `_is_gh_permanent_failure`, so `gh_retry` skips fail-fast and runs all 5 attempts with 1/2/4/8 s backoff, each attempt making one job-token call and one PAT call; minimax, luna and glm add that a PAT rate limit never matches `_is_gh_rate_limit`, so the alert, breaker and wait are skipped, and glm adds that the final `::error::`/`::warning::` excerpt names the job token's 502 instead of the PAT failure; severity disagreement: sonnet rated NIT (confidence 3, narrow trigger, at most 8 extra calls, and the read fails anyway), while minimax, luna and glm rated MAJOR, so the highest is used.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1320-1324 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The comment "The job-token output and stderr are dropped so a wrapping gh_retry classifies only the PAT's result." is stale, because when the PAT also fails, lines 1359-1361 return the job token's stderr and rc.
  WHY: Nothing breaks at runtime, but a future editor who trusts the comment could misread or "fix" the both-fail path; the header comment (lines 1082-1090 / 1085-1090) already describes the behaviour correctly; all three reviewers agree on NIT.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1349-1351 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When both tokens fail, each `gh_retry` attempt makes two API calls (job token + PAT) instead of one, and the transient job-token error returned guarantees the full 5-attempt backoff ladder (15 s) runs.
  WHY: A persistent job-token 5xx during a PAT outage turns one polling read into 5 job-token calls and 5 PAT calls, which worsens the budget pressure #9888 targets; the reviewer reports this as the quantified consequence of the masking finding, not as a separate defect.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:_gh_read_run, lines 1320-1324, the comment "The job-token output and stderr are dropped so a wrapping gh_retry classifies only the PAT's result." | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The comment is stale: when the PAT also fails, lines 1359-1361 discard the PAT's stderr and return the job token's stderr and rc; the header comment (lines 1082-1090), agents.d/9888-gh-read-token-polling.md and changelog.d/9888-gh-read-fallback-hardening.md are correct.
  WHY: No runtime break; a maintainer could "fix" the both-fail branch back to returning the PAT error, which would bring back the PAT rate-limit alert, breaker trip and 600 s wait and break test_other_failure_with_pat_rate_limited_returns_the_job_token_error.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:_gh_read_run, lines 1350-1361 (with gh_retry lines 2858-2865 and _is_gh_permanent_failure line 1800) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: In the reason=error both-fail branch, the PAT's stderr is always discarded, even for permanent PAT errors (HTTP 404/400/401/422, "Bad credentials"), not only for the PAT rate limit the code comment describes.
  WHY: `gh_retry` never matches `_is_gh_permanent_failure`, so it retries up to GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS (5) with 1/2/4/8 s backoff and its final excerpt shows the job token's 502; the trigger is narrow, the cost is at most 8 extra calls, and the read fails anyway.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:lines 1350-1361 in `_gh_read_run`, in conjunction with `gh_retry` lines 2797, 2813-15, 2858-2865 and `_is_gh_permanent_failure` line 1800 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When the PAT also fails after a reason=error job-token failure, line 1359 discards the PAT's stderr and lines 1360-1361 replay the job token's `err_text`/`${rc}`, hiding permanent PAT failures (404, 401 "Bad credentials", 422, "Resource not accessible") from `_is_gh_permanent_failure` and PAT rate limits from `_is_gh_rate_limit`.
  WHY: A transient job-token 5xx plus a broken PAT costs five attempts (5 job-token + 5 PAT calls, ~15 s backoff) ending in `::error::gh command failed after 5 attempts`, with no fail-fast, Telegram alert, breaker trip or reset wait.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:lines 1320-1324 (comment block above the `reason=error` branch in `_gh_read_run`) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The comment claims gh_retry classifies only the PAT's result, but lines 1360-1361 replay the job token's stderr/rc when the PAT fails too, which contradicts the header comment (lines 1082-1090).
  WHY: No runtime break; it misleads future editors and hides the defect above.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:_gh_read_run, lines 1350-1361 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When the job-token read fails with an unclassified error and the PAT fallback also fails, the helper discards the PAT's error and returns the job-token error; the comment at lines 1322-1324 wrongly says `gh_retry` classifies only the PAT's result.
  WHY: A rate-limited PAT makes `gh_retry` skip its rate-limit wait, alert and breaker and retry both tokens up to five times; permanent PAT errors are masked as well, so `gh_retry` cannot fail fast.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:`_gh_read_run` lines 1350-1361 (PAT fallback in the `reason=error` path), interacting with `gh_retry` lines 2858 and 2867 and `_is_gh_permanent_failure` line 1798 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

  WHY: 5 job-token calls plus 5 PAT calls per read during a PAT outage worsen #9888's budget pressure; the per-attempt cost is documented at lines 1348-1349, and the reviewer reports this as the quantified consequence of the finding above, not a separate defect.
